primary.title: Tata Sons' Monday meet gets Bombay HC nod
primary.description: The Bombay High Court on Friday allowed Tata Sons to proceed with its November 30 board meeting, refusing urgent relief sought by two Tata Trusts that challenged the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as executive chairman for a third five-year term.A bench of Justice Abhay Ahuja said any decision taken at the meeting would remain subject to the court's final orders. It also directed Tata Sons and the other respondents, including six of its directors, to file their replies to the two suits and scheduled the next hearing for January 18, 2027.The ruling allows the board meeting to go ahead as planned, even as the legal challenge to Chandrasekaran's reappointment remains pending. The trusts had sought a stay or deferment of the meeting, besides asking the court to restrain Chandrasekaran from exercising his casting vote if nominee directors were divided on a resolution."We are not granting any relief today. Let the meeting (on November 30) go on as per schedule. Any outcome of the meeting would be subject to our final orders," the court observed.The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and the RD Tata Trust filed the suits on Thursday against Tata Sons and six of its directors, arguing that the September 17 board resolution reappointing Chandrasekaran was invalid. They contended that it did not secure the affirmative vote required under Article 121 of the company's Articles of Association.The trusts have also sought damages of Rs 50 crore and Rs 15 crore, respectively, along with 18% annual interest.Tata Sons opposed the plea to defer the meeting. Its counsel, Harish Salve, told the court that the board needed to meet to comply with a Reserve Bank of India directive requiring the company to inform the central bank by December 12 of its decision on the mandated listing.Representing the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust, Abhishek Manu Singhvi argued that the RBI deadline was being used to create artificial urgency around the meeting.(With inputs from PTI)

primary.title: Tata Sons' Monday meet gets Bombay HC nod
primary.description: The Bombay High Court on Friday allowed Tata Sons to proceed with its November 30 board meeting, refusing urgent relief sought by two Tata Trusts that challenged the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as executive chairman for a third five-year term.A bench of Justice Abhay Ahuja said any decision taken at the meeting would remain subject to the court's final orders. It also directed Tata Sons and the other respondents, including six of its directors, to file their replies to the two suits and scheduled the next hearing for January 18, 2027.The ruling allows the board meeting to go ahead as planned, even as the legal challenge to Chandrasekaran's reappointment remains pending. The trusts had sought a stay or deferment of the meeting, besides asking the court to restrain Chandrasekaran from exercising his casting vote if nominee directors were divided on a resolution."We are not granting any relief today. Let the meeting (on November 30) go on as per schedule. Any outcome of the meeting would be subject to our final orders," the court observed.The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and the RD Tata Trust filed the suits on Thursday against Tata Sons and six of its directors, arguing that the September 17 board resolution reappointing Chandrasekaran was invalid. They contended that it did not secure the affirmative vote required under Article 121 of the company's Articles of Association.The trusts have also sought damages of Rs 50 crore and Rs 15 crore, respectively, along with 18% annual interest.Tata Sons opposed the plea to defer the meeting. Its counsel, Harish Salve, told the court that the board needed to meet to comply with a Reserve Bank of India directive requiring the company to inform the central bank by December 12 of its decision on the mandated listing.Representing the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust, Abhishek Manu Singhvi argued that the RBI deadline was being used to create artificial urgency around the meeting.(With inputs from PTI)
